proposals.name: Cornell Township Fire Millage Renewal Proposal
proposals.description:
Shall the previous voted increase in the tax limitation on general ad valorem taxes within Cornell Township, Delta County, imposed under Article IX, Sec. 6 of the Michigan Constitution, be renewed at 1 mill ($1.00 per $1,000 of taxable value) for a period of 10 years, 2028 to 2037 inclusive, for the purpose of operations, maintenance, building, updating equipment, including personnel protective equipment, and training of firemen?
The estimated revenue generated from the 1.0 mills that will be…
proposals.ballotLanguage:
Shall the previous voted increase in the tax limitation on general ad valorem taxes within Cornell Township, Delta County, imposed under Article IX, Sec. 6 of the Michigan Constitution, be renewed at 1 mill ($1.00 per $1,000 of taxable value) for a period of 10 years, 2028 to 2037 inclusive, for the purpose of operations, maintenance, building, updating equipment, including personnel protective equipment, and training of firemen?
The estimated revenue generated from the 1.0 mills that will be collected in the first year that the millage is authorized and levied will be $ 30,871.72.
proposals.officialTitle: CORNELL TOWNSHIP FIRE MILLAGE RENEWAL PROPOSAL
proposals.yesVote: A YES vote continues the existing levy of 1 mill for 10 years — generally no increase over what you pay now, plus the restored or added amount described.
proposals.noVote: A NO vote lets the current millage expire; the service it funds would need cuts or other revenue.
proposals.conservativeView: Renewals are the least disruptive way to keep a service funded, but every renewal is a chance to ask whether the service is delivering value. Watch for "renewal" proposals that quietly restore Headlee rollbacks — that is a tax increase.
proposals.progressiveView: Keeps an existing, voter-approved service funded at the same rate with no new tax.

proposals.name: Escanaba Area Public Schools Operating Millage Proposal
proposals.description:
This proposal will allow the school district to levy the statutory rate of not to exceed 18 mills on all property, except principal residence and other property exempted by law, required for the school district to receive its revenue per pupil foundation allowance.
Shall the limitation on the amount of taxes which may be assessed against all property, except principal residence and other property exempted by law, in Escanaba Area Public Schools, Delta and Marquette Counties, Michigan, be…
proposals.ballotLanguage:
This proposal will allow the school district to levy the statutory rate of not to exceed 18 mills on all property, except principal residence and other property exempted by law, required for the school district to receive its revenue per pupil foundation allowance.
Shall the limitation on the amount of taxes which may be assessed against all property, except principal residence and other property exempted by law, in Escanaba Area Public Schools, Delta and Marquette Counties, Michigan, be increased by 2.6061 mills ($2.6061 on each $1,000 of taxable valuation) for a period of 6 years, 2026 to 2031, inclusive, to provide funds for operating purposes; the estimate of the revenue the school district will collect if the millage is approved and levied in 2026 is approximately $170,500 (this millage is to restore millage lost as a result of the reduction required by the Michigan Constitution of 1963 and will be levied only to the extent necessary to restore that reduction)?
proposals.officialTitle: ESCANABA AREA PUBLIC SCHOOLS OPERATING MILLAGE PROPOSAL
proposals.yesVote: A YES vote raises the levy back to the originally authorized 18 mills, overriding the Headlee Amendment rollback — this is a tax increase over the current rate.
proposals.noVote: A NO vote keeps the current, rolled-back rate in place.
proposals.conservativeView: The Headlee Amendment is a constitutional taxpayer protection that limits how fast property-tax revenue can grow. Overriding it raises taxes above what the constitution would otherwise allow.
proposals.progressiveView: Restores funding that inflation and Headlee rollbacks have eroded so existing services can continue.
